correctness.rationale: Finite-dimensional linear isometry group is compact; invariant inner-product averaging conjugates its Lie algebra to a compact subalgebra g⊆so(5), whose commuting skew operators admit at most two independent real rotation planes (maximal abelian dimension≤2). Any compact real Lie algebra of dimension exactly five is either abelian R5 or su2⊕R2, both containing abelian subalgebra dimension≥3; hence 5 cannot embed. Rosenthal 1986 Theorem 3(a) bounds any non-Euclidean five-dimensional space by dim≤(5−1)(5−2)/2=6, so 7,8,9 impossible while Euclidean dim=10. On X(d1,...,dm) real ℓ1-direct sum of Euclidean blocks, extreme-point components force connected isometries to preserve each block, giving product SO(dj) and Lie dimension ∑dj(dj−1)/2. Independently enumerated partitions 5 with corresponding exact values [0,1,2,3,4,6,10] and explicit witnesses.
